name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,352

clue.text: Top methods becoming pronounced in Chinese artist

indicators.note: once the words are spoken rather than spelt, we keep only their sound

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written here with an I for the 1
ways, as in methods, said twice over

explanation.surface: Someone discusses the best techniques that made a Chinese painter famous.
explanation.walkthrough: AI WEIWEI is pronounced roughly 'eye way-way': A1 is top quality, and ways are methods.
explanation.definitionFit: Ai Weiwei is a famous contemporary Chinese artist and political activist, known for installations.

clue.text: A refusal to accept advice in rival religious authority

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in

blocks.note: a tip is a piece of advice

explanation.surface: A church leader won't take any advice from a rival authority.
explanation.definitionFit: An antipope is a person set up as pope in opposition to the canonically elected one.

clue.text: Desire to defend a bishop close to holy covenant

indicators.note: defending something means standing guard around it
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Wishing to protect a bishop who keeps close to a sacred agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: RR stands for Right Reverend, the formal style of an Anglican bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee or binding promise, a kind of covenant or formal undertaking.

clue.text: Beginnings of international rejection are quite injurious for Saddam, say

definitions.note: an example: a noun for a person from that country

indicators.note: the beginnings of words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Worldwide condemnation of a dictator is doing him real harm.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddam Hussein ruled Iraq, so he is an example of a native of that country.

clue.text: Shadowy official activated in emergencies

indicators.note: letters that are activated are stirred into motion and moved

explanation.surface: A mysterious official springs into action whenever there is a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence grise is a powerful adviser who wields influence behind the scenes, unseen and unofficial.

clue.text: Plant left in part of field

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: cover is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: A plant has been abandoned in a corner of a farmer's field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' suggests farming, but the part of the field is a cricket position, cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover is a low-growing leguminous herb with three-lobed leaves, often found in pasture.

clue.text: Specialist in stopping admissions?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone expert at turning people away or halting confessions
setter's reading: fitting the devices that keep people from getting in

explanation.walkthrough: Admissions suggests confessions or a door policy, but the specialist makes what bars entry to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and fits locks, whose whole purpose is preventing unwanted entry.

clue.text: Stomach a very uppity threatening look

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: A as written, V for very
to lour is to scowl or look menacing

explanation.surface: Someone can tolerate a really arrogant, menacing glare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' reads as a verb, to put up with, but the definition is the noun: guts.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the stomach for something means courage, and valour is bravery in the face of danger.

clue.text: Routes mentioned in Greek island

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so only its sound counts

explanation.surface: Travel routes on a Greek island get discussed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is the largest of the Dodecanese islands in the Aegean, belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Note end of summer sport in traditional area of ground

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

blocks.note: te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note about the late-summer sport played at a traditional sports ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracing is the stepped standing area at British football grounds, the traditional place for fans before all-seater stadiums.

clue.text: With day fading, idol facing riot breaking out in festivity

indicators.note: something fading disappears, so it is taken away
breaking out scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: As the day ends, a pop idol confronts a rioting crowd at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Glorification can mean a joyful celebration or festive praise, so a festivity in a broad sense.

clue.text: Source of music in Purcell opera

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Talk of where the music comes from in an opera by Henry Purcell.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a bowed string instrument, so a source of music in an orchestra.

clue.text: Fool curtailed trade in confection

indicators.note: curtailed means the tail, the final letter, is cut off

blocks.note: a prat is a fool in British slang
one's line of work is one's trade

explanation.surface: A dessert called a fool has had its trade cut short by a rival sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A fool is also a creamy fruit pudding, which makes it look like part of the confectionery theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Praline is a sweet made of nuts cooked in caramelised sugar, a classic confection.

clue.text: Dim old boy certain to tour college

indicators.note: touring something means going all the way round it

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for a former pupil

explanation.surface: A not-too-bright former pupil is determined to visit his old college.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something faint, unclear or hard to make out.

clue.text: Piano? It stuck out as quiet

definitions.note: the answer is an imperative phrase, so quiet is read as the command 'Quiet!' rather than an adjective, which is fair since both shush someone

indicators.note: letters put out of place no longer keep their order

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a piano with a key that stuck out, wanting it quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' looks like the musical instruction for softly, so a definition of quiet, but it is anagram fodder. The definition is the command Quiet!
explanation.definitionFit: Put a sock in it is a colloquial British phrase telling someone to stop talking or be quiet.

clue.text: Irritable writer, around 50, among names raised

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it
a thing among others is placed in their midst
raised in a down entry means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A grumpy author in his fifties finds himself among raised names.
explanation.definitionFit: Splenetic means bad-tempered or spiteful, from the old idea that the spleen caused ill humour.

clue.text: Brave leader upset over child, say

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means turned upside down

explanation.surface: A courageous leader is distressed over a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' looks like an adjective, but a brave is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Geronimo was an Apache war leader, so a leader of braves, Native American warriors.

clue.text: In addition to a sign of inflation, a sign of slump

indicators.note: the first sign of something is where it starts, its opening letter

blocks.note: a swelling or swell is a sign of being inflated

explanation.surface: Economic jargon: indicators of inflation along with signs of recession.
explanation.walkthrough: The parallel phrasing suggests two economic signs; the first is a swell, the second just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As well as is a phrase meaning besides or in addition to.

clue.text: Torpor from two drinks taken round quiet English ship

indicators.note: something taken round another wraps around it

blocks.note: a slug of spirits, then gin

explanation.surface: Lethargy comes from a couple of drinks taken around a silent English vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The two drinks are a slug and gin; only the second wraps round SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor and sluggishness both describe a state of physical or mental inactivity and lethargy.

clue.text: Here's, maybe, a grave intensity

blocks.note: first meaning: a grave is one kind of diacritic mark, offered here as an example
second meaning: stress or emphasis on a syllable

explanation.walkthrough: A grave reads as a burial place; it is the French mark, as in è.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is a type of diacritical mark over a letter, and the word also means stress or emphasis.

clue.text: To make and maintain contact in Australia is essential

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Keeping in touch is vital when you are in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and communicate with others, keeping a working connection.

clue.text: Greek character opposing Italian wine

blocks.note: a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person sets himself against an Italian vintage.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from the Tuscany region of Italy.

clue.text: Commend two pages in a range

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to range is to wander, to rove

explanation.surface: Praising a couple of pages within a mountain range or product line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' reads as a noun but is the verb to wander.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend something is to speak well of it, to approve of it.

clue.text: French writer ignoring posh sporting compatriot

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out

blocks.note: U means upper-class in British usage

explanation.surface: A French author pays no attention to his smart, athletic fellow countryman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alain Prost is a French Formula One champion, a sportsman sharing Proust's nationality.

clue.text: Remove fault almost kept in film

indicators.note: almost all of a word means it stops one letter short
something kept in another is held inside it

explanation.surface: A flaw has nearly been retained in a movie, so cut it.
explanation.definitionFit: To evict is to expel or remove a tenant from a property by legal process.

clue.text: Aisle I trod awkwardly with second gone to get view of organ?

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters fall out of their natural order
something gone has been taken away from the letters

blocks.note: the fodder before the letter is removed

explanation.surface: Walking clumsily down a church aisle to get a view of the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: The church setting makes 'organ' look like the instrument; here it is a newspaper, an organ of opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is an article stating a newspaper's own opinion, and a publication is called an organ.

clue.text: Ditch fish in river? The opposite

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, though the next words swap which goes inside
asks for the instruction to be turned around, so the containing roles are swapped

explanation.surface: A fish is dumped in a river, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' reverses the instruction: river in fish, not fish in river.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow excavation in the ground, as is a ditch.

clue.text: A French scout mistakenly embracing unionist that's smarmy

indicators.note: letters put down mistakenly are in the wrong order
to embrace is to wrap arms around something

explanation.surface: A French boy scout wrongly hugs a political unionist in an ingratiating way.
explanation.definitionFit: Unctuous describes someone excessively flattering and oily in manner, which is what smarmy means.
